where: next/tests/hooks/test_caller.py (DIFFERENTIAL_CHARACTERS and test_grammar_checker_agrees_with_the_allow_list); the classes are in _CALL_TEXT_RE, _SAFE and _QUOTED of next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/hooks/caller.py
problem: The differential test pins every character class only for ASCII and three code points beyond it: e-acute, U+0085 and U+2028 (DIFFERENTIAL_CHARACTERS). No other test puts a non-ASCII code point outside a quoted span. The only other non-ASCII code points inside one are e-acute, u-umlaut and i-umlaut. So widening or narrowing a character class with any other non-ASCII code point passes all 27 tests. I ran 1163 mutants of caller.py in a scratch copy of next/. These were killed: all 1032 per-character ASCII widenings and narrowings of the program's first class, its rest class, _SAFE, the separator, both pads and the quoted span; all 53 recorded mutations (the 49 and their variants); the pre-fix 'head required' revert; and every look-ahead, quantifier, structure and gate change. 70 survived. Two are equivalent mutants and need no test: [SAFE]*= changed to [SAFE]+= after (?!=), and the bare word's + changed to *. Neither differs from the current regex on any of 1,069,774 texts. The other 68 are real. (1) 54 mutants add one of U+00A0, U+1680, U+2002, U+202F, U+3000, U+FEFF, U+200B, U+4E2D or U+1F600 to the program first class, the program rest class, _SAFE, the separator, the leading blanks or the trailing blanks. (2) 13 mutants refuse one of those nine inside a quoted span, or refuse the range U+0100-U+2027, the zero-width characters U+200B-U+200F with U+FEFF, the surrogates, or U+10000-U+10FFFF. (3) One mutant compiles the gate with re.I. That lets 'vsdd survey ſ' (U+017F, long s), 'vsdd survey K' (U+212A, the Kelvin sign) and 'vsdd survey aİb' (U+0130) through both gates. The current regex is right on every code point: an exhaustive sweep of all 1,113,984 code points from U+0080, at nine positions, disagreed with the spec nowhere. The risk is low. The four shells and the runner's parser read non-ASCII characters as word characters. So a widened blank class is refused by the parsed gate wherever it would change the program, and elsewhere it only admits an odd argument. A narrowed quoted span fails safe, but it silently stops marking real calls, such as a quoted title with an emoji or CJK text. The gap predates this round. The fixer's claim that the differential 'pins every character class at every position' holds only for ASCII and the three sampled code points.
proposed_resolution: Change test_caller.py only. Add a test that checks every code point from U+0080 to U+10FFFF with _CALL_TEXT_RE alone. Each code point c must be refused in each of: '<c>x/vsdd survey', './a<c>b/vsdd survey', 'vsdd survey a<c>b', "vsdd survey a<c>='x'", 'vsdd<c>survey', '<c>vsdd survey', 'vsdd survey<c>' and "vsdd survey 'x'<c>". One text that holds every one of them inside a single quoted span must be accepted. Also send U+017F, U+212A, U+0130 and U+0131 in a bare word through is_vsdd_call and assert refusal; that catches a case-insensitive gate. I ran this test in a scratch copy. It adds about 4.6 s, passes on the current code and kills all 68 survivors. If 4.6 s is too slow, extend DIFFERENTIAL_CHARACTERS instead: add one code point from each Unicode general category, every Zs, Zl, Zp and Cf code point, a surrogate, an astral code point and the four case-folding letters. Then re-run the non-ASCII mutants.
